title: Prove odd-division obstruction for canonical Clifford decoding
body:
This scoped negative result proves that the full four-qubit canonical Clifford decoder needs odd division at every odd width f>=13 and every f>=14 with f=2 modulo 4. A finite exact Gaussian-dyadic linear circuit cannot implement that map on arbitrary observations. **No new kappa** follows; all five assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged.

[Proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9321c67e29c3c41a188154bc5c2add7d7802b694/research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction/PROOF.md) · [Exact certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9321c67e29c3c41a188154bc5c2add7d7802b694/research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction/RESULT.json) · [Checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9321c67e29c3c41a188154bc5c2add7d7802b694/research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction/verify.py) · [Source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9321c67e29c3c41a188154bc5c2add7d7802b694/research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction/SOURCE-PINS.json) · [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19727535).

For one explicit Gram eigenvalue `M/2^e`, the proof shows that M is odd and greater than one throughout each infinite width family. If D clears the odd denominators of the Gram inverse, then M divides D. If D clears those of the canonical least-squares decoder, then M divides D squared.

| Width | Selected numerator M | Necessary divisor of decoder D |
|---|---:|---:|
| 13 | 470624175 | 498015 |
| 14 | 5741614935 | 30378915 |

These are necessary divisors, not sufficient denominators for the complete map. Other spectral blocks and projectors can add factors. The explicit example `A=(1,2)^T` has a non-dyadic canonical inverse but a dyadic noise-free left inverse. Thus this result does not exclude every exact left inverse, restricted input contract, subalphabet or approximate decoder. Widths divisible by four are outside scope.

The exact base is `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. Ali Romman (@aliromman), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, produced this proof and checker. [PR #7788](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7788)'s [odd spectral proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/PROOF.md) and [PR #7789](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7789)'s [Bell spectral proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a5aa2ae21ae68338390f584b8fca58ecba0df409/research/clifford-bell-sector-spectrum/PROOF.md) supply the full-rank spectral identification and positive certificates. [PR #7772](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7772) supplies [generic Gaussian operations](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1398fbdca3536389d8ac3c8b3aaa408f03e8f6c2/research/clifford-threshold-conditioning/verify.py).

Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplies the retained character projection; alephnan (@alephnan) supplies the inherited Pauli/Gram framework. Their source links and table notices are in [Credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9321c67e29c3c41a188154bc5c2add7d7802b694/research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction/CREDITS.md). Nick's related [PR #7269](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7269) gives [exact denominator budgets for real helper pairings](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7de4bd6bd4a6f7fae59b90c941ae5a3b9b3e652d/research/odd-budget-helper-capacity/PROOF.md). That capacity theorem is not a consumed dependency or independent check of this result. Localization and valuation arithmetic are classical.

Local CPython 3.12.16, standard library only, passes both registered modes. Each takes about 0.14 seconds. The checks cover two symbolic valuation certificates, two exact positive Bernstein expansions, 89 finite widths, the two complete first-width factorizations, six rejecting controls and two scope/positive controls. A separate literal 24-by-24 one-qubit Gram inverse has common denominator 45; both inverse products pass all 1,152 scalar entries. The checker authenticates eight retained files.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-odd-division-obstruction --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected markers:

```text
PASS_CLIFFORD_ODD_DIVISION_OBSTRUCTION
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
```

AST parsing, tabnanny, whitespace, committed bytes, source history and modes pass. Official export/input checks and both serial read-only, Git-free replays with an empty PATH pass without changing file hashes or modes. Timings establish timeout headroom only. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44473362856/job/135387918702) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

The spectral identifications remain mathematical inputs. Their full suites and the table archive are not rerun. No full four-qubit inverse, Lean, independent human/formal acceptance, physical realization or complete caller calculation is supplied. Odd division, precision, movement, storage and restoration remain unpriced. The next questions are sufficient denominators for the full canonical map and the existence of a different Gaussian-dyadic left inverse.

Live handoffs, fresh open/closed PRs and source/semantic searches showed no observed competing claim at this boundary. Cached searches omit unpublished work and many sparse local notes; they are not novelty certificates. This adds one isolated research package and changes no shared implementation or selected record.
